title: P-MoVE: Performance Monitoring and Visualization with Encoded Knowledge
problem: HPC systems lack a unified framework for monitoring and visualizing performance data across heterogeneous components from different vendors while providing real-time insights without system overhead.
motivation: Creating accurate digital twins of HPC systems enables better performance understanding, optimization, and management of complex heterogeneous computing environments.
method: P-MoVE uses a structured knowledge base that organizes how to monitor different vendors' hardware components. An abstraction layer (a translator that converts different vendors' data formats into one common format) lets measurements from any manufacturer flow into the system. It then runs continuous cache-aware roofline modeling—a calculation that predicts the maximum speed the system can achieve based on how fast data moves between fast local memory and slow main memory—to show performance bottlenecks in real time without adding system overhead.
key_novelty: Combining a structured knowledge base designed for high-performance computing with a translation layer so a single monitoring system works across different manufacturers' hardware.
contributions: Open-source framework for monitoring and visualizing live and recorded HPC performance data with real-time visualization capabilities
HPC-specific knowledge base built on ontology with system probing for metric sampler configuration and linked-data connections
Abstraction layer enabling low-level profiling across heterogeneous components from different vendors
Live cache-aware roofline modeling for real-time performance analysis without system overhead
primary_theme: HPC performance monitoring and digital twin framework
